children: By Rupert Steiner

Good morning. I'm Rupert Steiner, Barron's London Bureau Chief. You might see my name pop up in your inbox occasionally to help you make sense of market moves when Callum Keown is otherwise engaged. So let's dive in!

On day two of what is typically the gloomiest month of the year for markets, there are slim pickings to lift the spirits. All three major indexes are on track to open lower today and, as my colleague George Glover explains, the turmoil surrounding soaring bond yields hasn't eased. Another jump in oil prices after fresh strikes in the Middle East hasn't helped.

But there were two shining beacons overnight lighting a more positive path for markets. Dell stock jumped after earnings came in well ahead of expectations-and it's not the only tech stock having a good morning, coding platform GitLab was up 21% at time of writing and here's why.

Watch out later for Broadcom earnings after the bell. The stock has had a rough three months-falling 22% since disappointing on guidance for chip sales in its last update-and remains a key barometer of the AI trade that has driven markets for most of this year.
Have a great day.
P.S. Feel free to get in touch with any thoughts and comments.

? Dell boosts annual sales outlook on surging server demand

Dell Technologies raised its annual revenue forecast by $25 billion, to $192 billion, fueled by massive demand for servers that run AI tasks. The company exited the quarter with a record $95 billion backlog in its AI server business. COO Jeff Clarke noted that in the past 12 months, Dell has booked more than $130 billion in server orders as IT environments shift from cost centers to value drivers.
🛢? Chevron is expanding Venezuela oil production in Orinoco

Chevron is on the verge of signing a new deal to expand its oil production in Venezuela, people familiar with the transaction said. The oil giant is expected to add operations in the Orinoco belt, an area of Venezuela known for its vast reserves of heavy crude oil. This is while the U.S. government makes its own separate bet on Venezuela's oilfields.
🛡? Palo Alto results confirm AI is a tailwind for cybersecurity

Like last week's earnings for its competitor CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks' results confirm that cybersecurity stands out as a likely winner from AI among enterprise software providers. The security company beat expectations and raised its outlook as AI actually makes it easier to launch cyberattacks, making it a "tailwind" for the business.
? Atlanta Braves stock benefits from sale of L.A. Angels

Atlanta Braves Holdings stock rose after reports real estate billionaire and L.A. Rams owner Stan Kroenke is buying the L.A. Angels MLB team for a reported valuation of $4 billion, which would be a record. Climbing sports franchise valuations have boosted shares of the Braves, MLB's only publicly traded team with a market value of $3.3 billion.
💥 Elon Musk shared thoughts on power crisis, AI with G-20

SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk sees a "crisis of power," with more electricity needed for AI computers and the coming wave of robots. He has even suggested that SpaceX would start producing blades for power-generating turbines, something companies like Howmet Aerospace do. Musk shared other thoughts with the Group of 20. Read about it here.
💡 California utilities reprieved from wildfire legislation

California utilities like PG&E and Edison International sprang back after the California State Assembly kill wildfire legislation that left out Gov. Gavin Newsom's proposal to limit insurance companies from suing utilities over wildfire-related legal claims. Wall Street had broadly believed California utilities and their investors faced liability pressure.
